report.title: Q3 Sales Analysis
report.subtitle: Quarterly revenue, channel, and regional performance

sections.heading: Executive snapshot
sections.body: Q3 revenue closed at $18.4M, up 12.6% year over year and 4.1% above plan. Growth was concentrated in enterprise renewals and expansion deals, while new-logo acquisition slowed in late August. Gross margin compressed by 1.8 points because of higher fulfillment costs and deeper discounting in the self-serve channel.

sections.heading: Regional performance
sections.body: North America remained the largest region at $10.2M and grew 9% year over year. EMEA delivered the strongest growth at 19%, helped by three multi-year enterprise renewals. APAC finished 3% below plan after two large opportunities slipped into Q4.

sections.heading: Channel trends
sections.body: Enterprise direct sales accounted for 61% of Q3 revenue and produced the highest average contract value. Partner-led revenue grew 15% but had uneven conversion quality. Self-serve volume increased, yet average order value fell 8% as promotional campaigns attracted smaller customers.

sections.heading: Customer mix
sections.body: Existing customers generated 72% of revenue, driven by seat expansions and premium support add-ons. Net revenue retention improved to 116%. New customer acquisition was softer than expected, especially among mid-market prospects who delayed buying decisions because of budget reviews.

sections.heading: Risks and recommendations
sections.body: The main Q4 risks are continued margin pressure, a heavier reliance on expansion revenue, and pipeline slippage in APAC. Recommended actions are to protect enterprise renewal momentum, tighten discount approval rules in self-serve campaigns, and run a focused recovery plan for delayed APAC opportunities.
